rationale_overall: Every ticker in the 16-name watchlist (already at the max_watchlist_size cap) had thesis-supporting news within the trailing quarter: the AI mega-caps posted record results and strategic capacity commitments (Microsoft's 33% Azure growth and new Frontier enterprise-AI unit, Alphabet crossing $3T market cap, Nvidia's ~$100B OpenAI compute partnership); the rockets/spacecraft basket extended its backlog (Rocket Lab's new Synspective launch tranche and Mynaric stock-purchase agreement, AST SpaceMobile's FCC direct-to-device approval and Japan-subsidized satellite build-out); the quantum name advanced its roadmap (IonQ's Oxford Ionics acquisition nearing close plus a DOE MoU); the nuclear-fuel pair deepened utility/government ties (Centrus's Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power MoU and Piketon HALEU expansion, Cameco riding a red-hot uranium tape); the defense sleeve kept drawing inflows against the European rearmament buildup (ITA's late-September inflow, Lockheed's raised 2025 guidance); tanker exposure stayed supported by firm charter economics (Scorpio Tankers' new five-year STI Orchard charter); and the demographics/healthcare sleeve held up (CareTrust's continued capital deployment, Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci 5 software upgrades). None of this rises to a fundamental thesis breach or an unpriced peak-enthusiasm signal, and Pass-1 discovery across every named wave did not surface a candidate whose evidence cleared the bar to justify displacing a current holding at the 16-ticker cap. Net effect: no change to the watchlist's thematic shape this quarter.
